legend: Every February, the streets of Salvador surrender to the Carnaval, and no one feels it more than DJ Sandália, the legendary selector who rides the oldest trio elétrico circling the Campo Grande circuit. The folião crowd shouts song requests all night long, and DJ Sandália has carefully written down, for each of the N$$$N$$$ songs in the repertoire, an integer "weight" Pi$$$P_i$$$ that measures how badly the crowd wants to hear song i$$$i$$$.
To keep the party fair, DJ Sandália wants to pick the next song at random so that song i$$$i$$$ is chosen with probability exactly Pi/(P1+P2+⋯+PN)$$$P_i / (P_1 + P_2 + \dots + P_N)$$$.

There is just one problem: the trio's randomizer is a battered piece of hardware from the 1980s, and the only thing it knows how to do is to draw an integer uniformly at random from a given range. It cannot weight anything by itself; every draw it produces is perfectly uniform.

Working only with this uniform randomizer, DJ Sandália came up with the following strategy. First, choose a single integer K$$$K$$$ and build three arrays A$$$A$$$, B$$$B$$$ and C$$$C$$$, each of length N$$$N$$$. Then, to pick a song:
draw x$$$x$$$ uniformly from 1$$$1$$$ to N$$$N$$$;
draw y$$$y$$$ uniformly from 0$$$0$$$ to K$$$K$$$;
if y<Cx$$$y  \lt  C_x$$$, play song Ax$$$A_x$$$; otherwise, play song Bx$$$B_x$$$.

Help DJ Sandália choose K$$$K$$$ and the arrays A$$$A$$$, B$$$B$$$ and C$$$C$$$ so that this procedure plays song i$$$i$$$ with probability exactly Pi/(P1+⋯+PN)$$$P_i / (P_1 + \dots + P_N)$$$, for every song i$$$i$$$.
input: The first line contains a single integer N$$$N$$$ (1≤N≤1000$$$1 \leq N \leq 1000$$$), the number of songs.
The second line contains N$$$N$$$ integers P1,P2,…,PN$$$P_1, P_2, \dots, P_N$$$ (1≤Pi≤109$$$1 \leq P_i \leq 10^{9}$$$), the weight of each song.
output: On the first line, print a single integer K$$$K$$$ (0≤K≤1018$$$0 \leq K \leq 10^{18}$$$).
On the second line, print N$$$N$$$ integers A1,…,AN$$$A_1, \dots, A_N$$$ (1≤Ai≤N$$$1 \leq A_i \leq N$$$).
On the third line, print N$$$N$$$ integers B1,…,BN$$$B_1, \dots, B_N$$$ (1≤Bi≤N$$$1 \leq B_i \leq N$$$).
On the fourth line, print N$$$N$$$ integers C1,…,CN$$$C_1, \dots, C_N$$$ (0≤Ci≤K$$$0 \leq C_i \leq K$$$).

Your answer is accepted if, for every song i$$$i$$$, the probability that the described procedure plays song i$$$i$$$ equals Pi/(P1+⋯+PN)$$$P_i / (P_1 + \dots + P_N)$$$ exactly. Any valid answer will be accepted.
note: With a single song, K=4$$$K = 4$$$ and the only bucket points to song 1$$$1$$$ on both sides, so song 1$$$1$$$ is always chosen.
Here K=3$$$K = 3$$$. With the printed table, Pr[1]=14=P1S$$$\Pr[1] = \tfrac14 = \tfrac{P_1}{S}$$$ and Pr[2]=34=P2S$$$\Pr[2] = \tfrac34 = \tfrac{P_2}{S}$$$, so it is a valid answer.
Here K=3$$$K = 3$$$. The printed table gives Pr[1]=Pr[2]=14$$$\Pr[1] = \Pr[2] = \tfrac14$$$ and Pr[3]=12$$$\Pr[3] = \tfrac12$$$, matching Pi/S$$$P_i / S$$$. Any other valid table is also accepted.

为了让派对公平，DJ Sandália 希望随机选择下一首歌曲，使得歌曲 i$$$i$$$ 被选中的概率恰好为 Pi/(P1+P2+⋯+PN)$$$P_i / (P_1 + P_2 + \dots + P_N)$$$。
但存在一个问题：这辆 trio 的随机装置是 20 世纪 80 年代的一件破旧硬件，而它唯一会做的事情，就是从给定范围内均匀随机抽取一个整数。它无法自行对任何东西加权；它每次产生的抽取结果都完全均匀。
仅使用这个均匀随机装置，DJ Sandália 想出了如下策略。首先，选择一个整数 K$$$K$$$，并构造三个数组 A$$$A$$$、B$$$B$$$ 和 C$$$C$$$，它们的长度均为 N$$$N$$$。然后，要选择一首歌曲：
如果 y<Cx$$$y  \lt  C_x$$$，播放歌曲 Ax$$$A_x$$$；否则，播放歌曲 Bx$$$B_x$$$。
请帮助 DJ Sandália 选择 K$$$K$$$ 以及数组 A$$$A$$$、B$$$B$$$ 和 C$$$C$$$，使得对于每首歌曲 i$$$i$$$，该过程播放歌曲 i$$$i$$$ 的概率恰好为 Pi/(P1+⋯+PN)$$$P_i / (P_1 + \dots + P_N)$$$。
